newsitem.title: HONDURAS: Honduran police look for hundreds of escaped inmates.
newsitem.headline: Honduran police look for hundreds of escaped inmates.

text.p: Police on Tuesday searched for hundreds of prisoners who escaped from jail in northwestern Honduras following a deadly prison riot.
Some 380 prisoners were on the loose after breaking free from a prison late on Monday near the town of Santa Barbara, some 110 miles (180 km) northwest of the capital Tegucigalpa, police said.
Inmates angry at poor conditions and a slow judicial system in this Central American nation threw rocks at the guards and set fire to the jail before busting out.
One prisoner was killed during the melee, although police had no details about how he died. All 482 prisoners escaped but more than 100 were later captured, police said.

"People are protesting because they suspended our daily visits and we live in bad conditions, there is hardly any room to stand in here," one inmate who identified himself as Cristobal Sagastume told Honduran radio late on Monday.

Jails in this impoverished nation are overcrowded and a majority of the inmates are still awaiting trial years after their original offence. Legal experts say some have probably already served out their sentences.
The Santa Barbara jail had space for 100 prisoners but was home to nearly five times that amount.

Inmates also rioted and set a fire on Monday to another Honduran jail in the town of Trujillo, some 180 miles (290 km) north of the capital, but officials said no prisoners had escaped or were injured.

"They are burning the building, throwing rocks at the windows and at the roof of the hospital," Julieta Sanchez, a nurse at a hospital adjacent to the Trujillo jail, told Honduran radio late on Monday.
